headline: Expects a credit market downward cycle over the next one to two years as high interest rates, falling property prices and cost-of-living pressures combine into a 'perfect storm' not seen for several generations
reasoning: Steve Laidlaw notes that interest rates are at their highest in roughly 15 years, meaning many borrowers have never experienced such levels. He observes that newer home buyers are seeing equity declines of around 5%, potentially reaching 10% or even 15% according to some pundits, though he is less pessimistic. Combined with cost-of-living pressures and budget impacts, he characterises the environment as a perfect storm for the housing market. He expects overall lending demand to moderate and is boosting support teams in preparation for a credit downturn, while noting that strong prior house price appreciation provides significant equity buffers for most banks.
quote: it is a perfect storm. I think in terms of the housing market and one we haven't seen for several generations. I expect the bank is in a very strong position as I think all banks are in Australia. The sheer increase in housing prices over the last several years means there is a lot of equity for most customers and for most banks a significant buffer in terms of any issues with respect to credit. Having said that, we are seeing increasing requirements to support a number of our customers through meeting their repayments because of the combination particularly around the high interest rates and some of the cost of living pressures. And being a customer owned bank, we can tend to be a little bit more generous and empathic around that level of support. So we're certainly boosting our teams and getting ready for what we see is a potential downward cycle around credit markets.
episode_title: People First Bank bets big on digital

headline: Lending growth running ~8% above system but moderation now underway as rate expectations, cost-of-living and budget pressures weigh on demand
reasoning: People First Bank grew its lending book at approximately 8% over the prior year, well above system, and has had a good start to the current financial year. However, Laidlaw signals that demand is now moderating as expectations of further rate rises, cost-of-living issues and budgetary pressures feed through to overall lending activity. He expects the market-wide lending growth base to decline over the next year or two as borrowers remain hesitant about where house prices will land.
quote: We had good growth last year, certainly well above system around 8% of growth in our lending book. We've had a good start to this financial year as well, though we are now starting to see some moderation in demand. Clearly, you know, the expectation of further rate rises, the budgetary pressures, cost of living issues is certainly starting to play into overall lending demand.
episode_title: People First Bank bets big on digital

headline: Digital banking adoption accelerating: branch closures driven by overwhelming customer demand for digital, with younger demographics treating non-digital service as a failure; heavy investment in AI for fraud and scam protection now a key priority
reasoning: Steve Laidlaw describes a major shift in customer behaviour, with 99% of banking transactions now digital and growing. Younger customers view the need to call or visit a branch as a service failure, forcing banks to prioritise digital investment. People First Bank released a new digital banking app built on Backbase technology. The bank closed 15 branches in 2025 to reallocate capital toward digital and fraud-protection investment, while maintaining around 55 branches. AI is being deployed proactively to combat scams and fraud, which he flags as a significant and growing area of required investment.
quote: It's really one based on the demand of our customer base. You know, we have a limited amount of capital that we can invest into various services and overwhelmingly the demand is for improved digital experiences by our customers. We still have a very strong branch network around Australia, around 55 branches and we'll continue to have one for the, you know, quite a long time. It's an important part of our service proposition, but you need to act in the interests of your customers as a whole. And overwhelmingly they are requiring and expecting an improved digital experience and also greater protections from scams and fraud. So you need to balance the investment pool across the branch footprint and the digital offering. And again, that shift is continuing to head towards the digital experience.
episode_title: People First Bank bets big on digital
